Insight


# August 2026 U.S. National Consumer Credit Trends Report


October 05, 2026


**Highlights:**


-


As of August 2026, total U.S. consumer debt reached $18.45 trillion, representing a 3.0% year-over-year increase, with mortgage debt maintaining a dominant 74.2% share of the total market.


-


Total non-mortgage debt reached $4.76 trillion, with auto loans and leases accounting for 36.4% and student loans making up 26.9% of the non-mortgage portfolio.


As of August 2026, the monthly Equifax Consumer Credit Trends Report showed that total U.S. consumer debt was $18.45 trillion, up 3.0% from August 2025. Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.69 trillion, a 74.2% share of total consumer debt, while non-mortgage consumer debt totaled $4.76 trillion, with 36.4% of non-mortgage consumer debt attributable to auto loans and leases, and 26.9% attributable to student loans.


Outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 3.3% from August 2025, to $1.73 trillion in August 2026.


Outstanding balances on U.S. bankcards decreased slightly versus the prior month to $1.12 trillion in August 2026, up 3.6% from August 2025. Average bankcard utilization stood at 20.3%, which is a slight decrease from 20.9% in August 2025.


#### Consumer Credit Observations:


-


As of August 2026, total U.S. consumer debt was $18.45 trillion, up 3.0% from August 2025.


-


Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.69 trillion, making up 74.2% of total U.S. consumer debt.


-


First mortgages were 94.9% of mortgage debt outstanding.


-


Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOCs) were 3.3% of mortgage debt outstanding.


-


Non-mortgage debt totaled $4.76 trillion in August 2026 and broke down into:


-


-


36.4% from auto loans and leases.


-


26.9% from student loans.


-


24.6% from credit card balances.


-


12.1% from other products.

Download the[August 2026 National Consumer Credit Trends Report](https://assets.equifax.com/marketing/US/assets/portfolio-credit-trends-sept26.pdf) now for the latest full dataset.


**Auto Loans and Leases Observations:**


-


Total outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 3.3% from August 2025 to $1.73 trillion.


-


The number of outstanding accounts in August 2026 was 87.3 million, a 0.4% increase year-over-year.


-


The severe balance delinquency (60+ days past due) rate in August 2026 was 1.32%, which is 22 basis points down from August of last year.


**Bankcard Portfolio Observations:**


-


Outstanding balances on bankcards increased 3.6% from August 2025 to $1.12 trillion.


-


The number of outstanding accounts was 601.9 million in August 2026, a 3.1% increase from August 2025.


-


The severe balance delinquency rate (60+ days past due) as of August 2026 was 2.71%, which is a 2 basis point decrease from August 2025 (2.73%).


-


Average bankcard utilization for August 2026 was 20.3%, compared to 20.9% in August of 2025.
